newsitem.title: JAPAN: Philippine minister says property fears unfounded.
newsitem.headline: Philippine minister says property fears unfounded.

text.p: Philippine finance minister Roberto de Ocampo said on Saturday Manila's financial markets were over-reacting to reports of an impending crash in the property market..

"The concerns raised in the financial markets, I would say are overblown. They had to do with some fluctuations in the stock market occasioned by speculation on real estate stocks," Ocampo said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television..
The Philippine Stock Exchange, one of the best performing in the region until about a month ago, began plunging after rumours gripped the market that two property firms were nearly bankrupt..
Despite repeated denials from the two companies as well as assurances from the Central Bank and government officials, investors have continued to hammer the market.
The real estate scare affected some bank stocks as well in the belief their loans to the property sector were high..
To the consternation of the Philippines' economic managers, some analysts drew a parallel with Thailand where an overheated property market affected financial markets..
"This reminds me of the time when people were comparing the Philippines with Mexico and they were wrong. Well, they are wrong again," de Ocampo said..
"Philippine banks are not overexposed. The loan portfolio of Philippine banks to the property sector is only about nine percent," he added..
This week the stock market made a technical rebound but analysts predicted investors would remain wary..
With foreign funds pulling out of the stock market, the peso had weakened slightly forcing the Central Bank to raise interest rates.
"The Central bank was able to give strong and effective warning to speculators and bring the markets back to a stable situation," de Ocampo said..
He said the Central Bank was able to effectively counter any attacks on the currency because of strong reserves.
On the Central Bank's decision last month to postpone a Yankee bond issue, de Ocampo said it was done because market conditions were not right.
De Ocampo said he expected the Philippines to get a credit upgrade soon.
"In the near future the Philippines will be upgraded which means our capability to go into the international capital markets will be better," he said.
